results.contract: Laravel has a separate authenticated verification-request flow; a validation rule alone does not fulfill it. No external email or DNS service is contacted in this evidence check.

optionReview.rationale: Domain mail infrastructure says nothing about which user controls an individual mailbox.
Repeating a syntax check does not demonstrate access to the mailbox.
A challenge ties successful completion to receiving mail at the address; syntax and DNS checks do not prove mailbox possession.
Normalization changes representation; it does not prove ownership.

results.contract: The authorization phase precedes validation completion and the action. The required debit/write atomicity belongs to the later application transaction, not this permission hook.

optionReview.rationale: The earlier authorize call cannot retroactively undo its committed side effect by returning a different value later.
Preparation runs even earlier and does not make the debit atomic with the write.
The later write can still fail after the debit has already been committed.
Authorization can run before later failures; an atomic transaction can commit the debit together with the successful operation.

results.contract: Form Requests expose separate rule and authorization boundaries. This is an architectural contract review, not a claim to execute a particular application policy.

optionReview.rationale: Input preparation does not replace explicit endpoint permission decisions.
Shared rule construction can be reused while each request owns the permission and requiredness decisions for its operation.
Data-format validation should not grant permission when either unrelated operation happens to be authorized.
Shared field formats do not establish permission for either operation.

results.contract: Session blocking coordinates participating requests through the configured cache lock store. This contract check does not claim a multi-process concurrency benchmark.

optionReview.rationale: The unlocked writer can still overlap the protected request, so both competing routes must participate.
A longer expiry does not serialize simultaneous updates.
Flash changes retention lifetime, not the concurrent read-modify-write race.
Session blocking uses a shared lock for the session so participating requests do not overlap their session read-modify-write work.

results.contract: The middleware supports targeted URI exemptions. Provider signature/replay verification is a separate application requirement and is not claimed to be exercised against a payment service.

optionReview.rationale: The external integration uses its own authenticated-message contract; the narrow exemption preserves browser-form protection elsewhere.
That broadens the exemption to browser forms and does not authenticate the sender.
A browser session token is not the provider integration credential and does not establish the webhook signature contract.
A sender can choose that field; it does not authenticate the message.
